summary: Streaming session resumes append duplicated trailing clause and omit closing punctuation after client socket migration behind corporate proxy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after an intermittent client socket migration (mobile->wifi) while connected through a corporate forward proxy, streaming responses resume but the last clause is duplicated and the closing punctuation (final period) is missing. Impact: user-visible corrupted final sentence in generated completions for chat/streaming flows. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east running redwood-7b-instruct pinned to v2026-02-22, customer using a browser client via an enterprise forward proxy that performs connection pooling and occasional HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrades. Steps to reproduce (customer): 1) Start a long-running streaming chat request over websocket. 2) Trigger network handover (cellular -> wifi) on client while proxy remains in path. 3) Observe reconnect/resume. Observed behavior: On reconnect the stream resumes and emits the remaining tokens, but the last clause is duplicated (e.g., "...and confirm appointment at 10am" becomes "...and confirm appointment at 10amand confirm appointment at 10am") and final punctuation is absent. Expected behavior: Single coherent concluding clause with proper punctuation.

Notes: this is not a full truncation — content is duplicated and concatenated with a missing delimiter. Customer provided HAR and a small recording of the session.
steps_to_reproduce: Open websocket streaming session to /v1/streams with model=redwood-7b-instruct and long prompt
Simulate client network handover while stream is active (client IP changes) behind enterprise forward proxy performing HTTP/2 multiplexing
Allow client to reconnect using same client-id/session token and resume stream
Inspect last 1-3 seconds of emitted tokens for duplication and punctuation loss

comments: Priya Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-02: Customer submitted HAR and video; says problem reproduces ~1/25 connections when on mobile handover behind corp proxy.
Ethan Liu (SRE) 2026-03-02: We've observed session id rebinding logs for this tenant during short-lived path migrations. Opening investigation to check idempotency mapping and streaming replay logic.
Nimbus Health (Customer) 2026-03-03: Happy to provide a test device and allow packet captures during an incident window. This is impacting clinical note quality in our triage flow.

Ethan Liu (SRE) 2026-03-04: Preliminary hypothesis: when the proxy performs connection pooling and reuses an upstream socket, our resume merge logic receives overlapping terminal fragments and concatenates them without re-inserting the expected delimiter. Reproducing a deterministic case in staging next.

Jonas Ortega (Eng) 2026-03-04: I can add extra guards to the resume merge path to detect overlapping token sequences and dedupe repeated suffixes. Need a failing test from customer traces to validate.
investigation_notes: Checked session-manager traces: client_id mapped to two close-to-simultaneous session objects during handover window (t=+400ms).
Resume algorithm log shows two resume fragments with identical tail tokens merged sequentially instead of being deduplicated.
Edge-proxy performed HTTP/2 stream reset and then reused an upstream socket for the new client connection — upstream connection id remained the same, which confused idempotency mapping.
No model-level repetition detected in serving-runtime token generation; duplication appears to occur in the resume/merge layer at the gateway.
Reproduced in staging with an emulated enterprise proxy that rebinds streams: duplication rate ~30% under our test harness; adding an overlap-detection reduces to 0%.
Potential risk: naive dedupe could remove legitimate repeated tokens in rare conversational patterns — need sequence-equality check only for final N tokens (configurable threshold).
Relevant artifacts: pcap (customer) stored in ticket attachments; internal trace IDs: trace-20260302-14-12a, trace-20260302-14-12b.
temporary_workaround: Ask clients to retry the full request on network change; for mobile SDKs, recommend single reconnection-per-handshake and avoid automatic resume when behind enterprise proxies until fix is rolled out.
resolution: In progress: engineering will ship a patch to the session resume merge logic that performs suffix-equality detection for the final 32 tokens and drops duplicates. Patch PR opened and linked. Plan: canary patch deployed to staging, then prod for dedicated tenants with scheduled maintenance. Post-deploy, monitor duplication metric and customer validation.
related_prs_and_rollout: Deployment plan: canary to 5% traffic on 2026-03-06, ramp to 100% by 2026-03-09 if no regressions
postmortem_followup: Add test harness scenario to CI that simulates connection pooling + client IP handover
Update streaming runbook to include guidance for enterprise proxies and recommended client SDK reconnection policies
Customer outreach: schedule validation window with Nimbus Health and provide patch notes
